original_question: Is the condition in which the brain's cerebral hemispheres are largely absent, and the remaining cranial cavity is filled with cerebrospinal fluid, classified as an open or closed neural tube defect (NTD)?

final_qi.question: Is the condition in which the brain's cerebral hemispheres are largely absent classified as an open neural tube defect (NTD)?
final_qi.long_answer: The congenital anomaly characterized by the near-complete absence of the cerebral hemispheres is anencephaly. Anencephaly arises from failure of closure of the rostral (cranial) end of the neural tube during primary neurulation. Because the neural tissue is left exposed without overlying skin or bone, anencephaly is classified in embryology and teratology texts as an "open" neural tube defect. Open NTDs (as opposed to closed/skin-covered defects) include anencephaly, myelomeningocele, and craniorachischisis. Therefore, the condition described is indeed classified as an open neural tube defect according to established biomedical consensus.

final_qi.question: Is the condition in which the brain's cerebral hemispheres are largely absent classified as a closed neural tube defect (NTD)?
final_qi.long_answer: The congenital condition in which most or all of the cerebral hemispheres (and often the overlying skull and scalp) are absent is termed anencephaly. Anencephaly results from failure of closure of the rostral (cranial) end of the neural tube during the third to fourth week of embryogenesis. By accepted embryological and clinical classification, anencephaly belongs to the group of open neural tube defects, in which neural tissue is exposed because it is not covered by skin or bone. Closed neural tube defects, in contrast, are characterized by a defect that is covered by skin (e.g., spina bifida occulta, lipomyelomeningocele). Therefore, describing anencephaly—or any condition marked by near-absence of the cerebral hemispheres due to neural tube non-closure—as a closed neural tube defect is inconsistent with established medical consensus.
